question: What does the IMD bulletin say about banana in Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu?
answer:
From the Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu bulletin issued 2026-09-11, for banana:

Banana · 5 months old · page 2:
“Prevailing wind speed is more than 10 km per hour along with light rainfall. Hence, five months old banana may be propped against lodging.”

Context from the same bulletin edition follows. These are separate source sections, not crop-specific matches or verified current official warnings. Printed warning dates and conditions are preserved; bulletin forecast dates do not extend their validity.

Weather forecast for next five days: (12.09.2026 to 16.09.2026) · page 1:
“According to district forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department for Coimbatore district, sky will be mostly cloudy. Light to Moderate rainfall is expected in Western Ghats regions of some places and Light rainfall is expected in other parts of Coimbatore. Maximum temperature is expected to be around 31-34°C. Minimum temperature is expected to be around 20-23°C. Morning relative humidity is expected to be around 80-90% and evening relative humidity is expected to be between 50-60%. Average wind speed is expected to be around 10-12 km per hour and the wind directions will be from South West direction.”

Weather Warning · page 2:
“12.09.2026 to 15.09.2026 : Thunderstorms & Lightning, Squall etc. 16.09.2026 : No Warning”

Weather Warning on Agriculture · page 2:
“Thunderstorms & lightning, squally wind is expected in some places and hence farmers are requested to stake banana crop which are more than five month old.”

SMS advisory: · page 3:
“ With the receipt of anticipated rainfall dry lands may be prepared for sowing millets and pulses during North East Monsoon.”

General · page 2:
“Drizzling or Light rainfall is expected in the western zone for the forth coming week. 15th & 16th September may get 15-20mm of rainfall in all three districts. Isolated places along the Western Ghats may receive thunderstorm. Hence, avoid trespassing and animal grazing near Western Ghats. Irrigation may be continued based on the soil moisture. Provide adequate draining to young crops.”

These are original English source excerpts, including their conditions. The bulletin is district guidance; it has not been validated for your individual field.
